newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rights groups slam Rwanda over civilian killings.
newsitem.headline: Rights groups slam Rwanda over civilian killings.

text.p: Two human rights groups said on Wednesday that Rwanda had not convincingly denied U.N. reports that its army had killed hundreds of civilians.

The New York-based Human Rights Watch and the Paris-based International Federation of Human Rights Leagues (FIDH) said they had written to Rwandan President Pasteur Bizimungu and Defence Minister Paul Kagame demanding that "they immediately order an end to massacres of civilians by the Rwandan Patriotic Army."

Rwanda this week dimissed as baseless reports by the United Nations and Amnesty International that its soldiers had killed more than 2,000 civilians in the past three months, saying those killed were not "innocent civilians" but armed militiamen.

"Such a vague and superficial reply cannot deny the extremely detailed inquiry report which lists the dates of incidents and the number of presumed victims area by area," Human Rights Watch and FIDH said in a joint statement.
"If such a totally inadequate response were to be maintained, it would clearly prove that Rwanda authorities do not take seriously complaints about human rights violations."
Amnesty said the Rwandan army had massacred civilians in Ruhengeri and Gisenyi prefectures, where most of the people are Hutu.

Hutus, who make up the majority of Rwanda's population, massacred hundreds of thousands of Tutsis in 1994. Many fled to Zaire, now the Democratic Republic of Congo, when the Hutu government was overthrown in 1994 after Rwandan exiles, mostly Tutsis, invaded from Uganda.
